title: The Unbearable Heaviness of Remembering
coreMove: Treat traumatic memory as body, story, record, and culture at once; neither doubt nor sympathy should turn uncertainty into erasure.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Documented childhood abuse can be inaccessible years later, so forgetting cannot be treated as disproof.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Linda Meyer Williams's adult follow-up to separate forgetting from evidence of no abuse.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Traumatic memory may begin as bodily terror and later integrate through therapy, movement, and support.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show Nancy's anesthesia trauma becoming coherent through mind, body, and relationship.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Shell-shock denial harmed veterans by framing injury as cowardice or weak character.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Treat World War I shell-shock labels as part of the injury rather than neutral description.

exampleSpecs.audience: teachers connecting trauma and public myth
exampleSpecs.stakes: German denial after World War I linked humiliation, weakness, and later militarized politics.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Connect social denial of war trauma to intolerance of vulnerability and political mythmaking.

exampleSpecs.stakes: False Memory Syndrome concerns are real, but backlash can erase evidence of traumatic amnesia.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hold suggestion risk and traumatic amnesia evidence without collapsing either side.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A 1994 study found traumatic memories more disorganized and changeable than positive memories.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the 1994 contrast to explain why messy traumatic recall needs interpretation, not instant dismissal.
